$comment: The skills in the kit that come from somewhere else. Vendored skills: `agent-setup vendor sync` copies each upstream skill into kit/<role>/skills/<name>/ (kit/developer/ unless the entry names a role), re-applies the frontmatter overrides below (description, compatibility, removeKeys) and writes one licence per source to that role's licenses/ folder. Never hand-edit a vendored skill folder: the next sync overwrites it. Change this file instead; `why` records the reason for every local patch. A repository's `pin` holds it at a reviewed commit instead of the upstream head, with its `why`. Overrides keep every skill valid under the Agent Skills spec (agentskills.io), so the kit loads in any agent that reads SKILL.md folders. Only sources whose licence allows redistribution are vendored.

taste-skill.why: Upstream's v2 rewrite of taste-skill is a different skill: 2.4 MB of gallery-site data, scripts that drive Chrome, and a description that claims dashboards and app screens, which v1 leaves to frontend and design-system. Held at the reviewed v1 commit until v2 is weighed against the kit's design skills with eval-routing and eval-outcomes.

skills.name: agent-browser
skills.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents (Chrome/Chromium via CDP, accessibility-tree snapshots with @eN refs). Use to visually verify frontend work: screenshots across viewports and devices, dark mode and reduced-motion emulation, console and page errors, axe accessibility audits, exploratory QA (dogfood). Also use to navigate sites, fill forms, click, extract data, log in, automate Electron apps, or access protected Vercel deployments.
skills.compatibility: Requires shell access and the agent-browser CLI (npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install). Agents without a shell can run `agent-browser mcp` as an MCP server instead.
skills.why: Upstream says "Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools", which can hijack plain web fetches; replaced with the browser-verification lane it serves in the kit. `hidden` is not an Agent Skills field: the official validator (skills-ref) fails the skill and claude.ai rejects it.
